test.name: macOS 27 empties the user temporary folder at a reboot

expected: after a reboot of this Mac the user temporary folder from confstr _CS_DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR holds no entry older than the boot, so the runtime root and socket under it must be created again (spec 0004 Follow-up for feature 6, reboot part only)
actual: after the reboot the user temporary folder held 127 top level entries and 0 of them were older than the boot, so a runtime root and socket left there before a reboot are gone and stacklyd must create them again, which the daemon already does at start and at each socket check
steps: The user rebooted this Mac; the boot time is 2026-10-20T23:03:54Z (`sysctl -n kern.boottime`, sec 1792537434).

Ran `getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR`: /var/folders/sx/35k0wvh13dg0cgpr19hnkjb80000gp/T/. The folder itself is the same one (birth 2026-07-14 12:30:34 local), so macOS keeps the folder and removes what is inside.

Listed its top level about an hour after the boot: 127 entries, and `find <temp> -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 ! -newermt @1792537434` finds 0 entries older than the boot; every entry was created after login.

No marker file was left before the reboot, so this record proves only that nothing from before the boot survived at the top level; the multi day idle cleanup with stacklyd running stays open in record 2026-10-19-when-macos-27-cleans-the-user-temporary-folder-t.json.
reviewer: Claude Opus 5.5 (lead session, for ojiepermana, who did the reboot)
